mission: Max Tegmark's MIT physics group asks: 'Are you excited about AI but concerned about humanity losing control of it?' Its main focus is mechanistic interpretability — figuring out, ideally automatically, how trained networks work — in order to diagnose, improve and ultimately guarantee AI trustworthiness, increasingly via formal verification ('guaranteed safe AI'). Tegmark also leads the Future of Life Institute. Founding year approximate (Tegmark dates the agenda to his 2018 'Intelligible Intelligence' talk).

key_work.title: Provably safe systems: the only path to controllable AGI
key_work.plain_summary: Tegmark & Omohundro argue AGI should be built to provably satisfy human-specified requirements, using AI-powered formal verification and interpretability.

key_work.title: Towards Guaranteed Safe AI
key_work.plain_summary: Multi-author framework: pair an AI with a world model, a safety specification and a verifier that proves the AI meets it.

key_work.title: Language Models Represent Space and Time
key_work.plain_summary: Found that LLMs contain linear internal maps of world geography and historical time — evidence of 'world models'.

key_work.title: Opening the AI black box: program synthesis via mechanistic interpretability (MIPS)
key_work.plain_summary: Automatically converts small trained networks into readable Python code that can then be verified.

key_work.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
key_work.plain_summary: A new neural architecture designed to be more interpretable than standard networks.

people.role: Group lead; professor of physics, MIT

warnings.text: Today's powerful AI systems are 'opaque black boxes, offering few guarantees that they will behave as desired' (group site).
Humanity could lose control of AI (group site); Tegmark has argued AGI without provable safety bounds should not be built.

recommendations.text: Diagnose, improve and ultimately guarantee AI trustworthiness through mechanistic interpretability (group site).
Re-implement extracted algorithms in architectures that can be formally verified — 'provably safe' AI.
Study mechanism design and game theory for multi-scale alignment.
